title: Dedicated capacity: staged fallback & priority quota decision brief
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers requesting reserved throughput guarantees vary widely in traffic patterns and GPU families. Current intake lacks a crisp decision surface relating SLA latency/availability targets to reserved throughput, GPU class, and scaling policies. That causes slow onboarding, repeated follow-ups, and occasional SLA miss when customer bursts exceed anticipated patterns.

Goal: Produce a concise decision brief and operational rubric that product, solutions, and concierge teams can use during intake to: 1) map customer SLA targets to recommended reserved throughput and GPU class, 2) define staged fallback policies (graceful degradation order: model-variant -> regional failover -> queued throughput -> customer-visible throttling), and 3) codify quota/prioritization matrices for multi-tenant dedicated pools so customers understand preemption and burst rules.

Scope: Non-bug intake triage for dedicated/reserved pools only (hosted API and Private deployments considered where behavior diverges). Deliverables include the decision brief, intake checklist additions, a sample SLA quote worksheet, and a draft of console messaging for fallback events.
decision_summary:
Adopt a three-tier fallback model + priority quota matrix:
1) Preferred: Reserve capacity mapped to GPU class (A/B/C tiers) based on sustained baseline RPS and 99th percentile latency target.
2) Staged fallback: when pool pressure > threshold, automatically shift requests by policy order: model-variant fallback (quantized/cheaper variant) -> regional replica routing -> burst queueing with bounded wait -> visible throttling and negotiated failover.
3) Priority quotas: customers assigned a priority score (Commitment, SLA band, security class) that configures preemption windows and burst credits.
This model balances predictability for enterprise contracts and graceful degradation to preserve best-effort availability.
tradeoffs: Conservative reserved throughput recommendations reduce risk of SLA breach but increase cost to customers; we will present optional burst credits to mitigate upfront sizing friction.
More aggressive automated fallbacks (switching to quantized variants) reduce costs and preserve latency but risk output quality regressions; require eval suites per customer to enable safe fallbacks.
Priority quota enforcement adds operational complexity and telemetry requirements; necessary for predictable fairness in shared dedicated pools.
planned_work: Write decision brief and intake rubric (PM) - deliverable D1
Prototype quota-priority scoring algorithm with weights for commitment, SLA, and security constraints (Eng) - task E1
Define GPU-class mapping table (capacity/latency baselines) with Performance team - task E2
Add intake checklist items and customer worksheet template (Solutions) - task S1
Create console copy and rollout alerts for staged fallback events (DX/Product) - task UX1
Create small-scale canary in Dedicated test cluster to validate fallback transitions and metrics (Eng) - task E3
acceptance_criteria: Decision brief reviewed and approved by Product, Eng (Serving runtime lead), and Solutions
Intake rubric added to concierge playbook and tested in two recent onboarding case studies
Quota-priority algorithm prototype produces stable priority assignments on historical customer traffic (sanity check on 6 months of booking data)
Fallback transitions are observable in console with clear reason codes and a post-mortem checklist
Documented mapping from SLA bands -> recommended reserved throughput (tokens/sec or rps) and GPU class ranges
risks_mitigation: Risk: Quality regressions when falling back to quantized variants. Mitigation: require per-customer eval prompt set and automatic quality regression alerting tied to Redwood Optimize evaluations.
Risk: Customers dispute priority scoring. Mitigation: transparent score breakdown with appeal path and manual override for enterprise contracts.
Risk: Mis-sized burst credits cause noisy neighbor incidents. Mitigation: cap burst window and monitor tail latency, enable auto-throttle if tail latency crosses safety threshold.
